extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political/philosophy essays; policymakers and educators interested in liberty and individuality
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical/essayistic argument about the value of individuality, originality, and liberty for human well-being and social progress, addressing when and how society should permit or restrain individual impulses and eccentricities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of impulses and conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong impulses and desires are not inherently perilous; they become dangerous only when not properly balanced by a strong conscience and governing will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate both vigorous impulses (energy) and a strong will/conscience so that natural feeling can be directed to good. Anti-pattern: treating strong desires as intrinsically evil and suppressing them wholesale; consequence is dullness or loss of capacity for good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuality as development
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuality is the cultivation and expression of a person's own developed nature — 'a person whose desires and impulses are his own... is said to have a character.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Society should encourage the development of each person's distinct character within limits. Allowing different persons to lead different lives produces richer human life and strengthens society as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit different lives within rights of others
rubrics_metrics.description: To give fair play to the nature of each, different persons should be allowed to lead different lives, in proportion to their needs for spiritual and moral development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restraint is justified to prevent harm to others, but preventing harmless diversity (restraint out of mere displeasure) dulls and blunts human nature. Institutions and public sentiment should tolerate diverse modes of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom as the permanent source of improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberty, by allowing many independent centres of improvement, is the unfailing and permanent source of social and moral progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage decentralized experimentation and individual initiative rather than enforcing uniform improvements by authority. Anti-pattern: forcing improvements on an unwilling people or imposing a single pattern for all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of originality and genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality (genius) is necessary for discovering new truths, commencing better practices, and preventing established beliefs and practices from degenerating into the mechanical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the 'soil in which genius grows' by allowing freedom of thought and action; eccentricity and nonconformity should be protected because they are often the first forms of improvement. Anti-pattern: social indifference that tolerates genius only in theory but not in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish justified restraint from needless suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an important difference between restraints imposed to prevent injury to others (legitimate) and restraints that prohibit things indifferent to others (illegitimate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain as much restraint as necessary to protect others' rights, but avoid restrictions that merely enforce conformity and extinguish harmless individuality, which yields no moral development except resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of the despotism of custom and public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The tyranny of custom and the current standard of approbation (which favors conforming, moderate tastes) tends to make mediocrity the ascendant power and crush individuality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and resist pressures of public opinion that enforce uniformity; foster pronounced individuality among intellectually and morally gifted persons to counterbalance mass mediocrity. Example: fashion-change sameness and the Chinese historical example of stagnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eccentricity as societal service
rubrics_metrics.description: In an age where conformity is the norm, mere non-conformity (eccentricity) performs a public service by breaking the tyranny of opinion and keeping open possibilities for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage eccentric behaviour so long as it doesn't infringe others' rights; regard eccentricity as often proportional to genius and moral courage rather than as mere vice. Anti-pattern: treating eccentricity as evidence of insanity or unfitness (judicial/medical persecution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate individuality within limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Human beings become noble and beautiful by cultivating individuality, but cultivation must be within the limits imposed by the rights and interests of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and social norms should seek the minimal compression necessary to prevent encroachment; excessive compression destroys valuable human development and the social benefits it yields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to ideals that demand uniform self-denial
rubrics_metrics.description: The Calvinistic (or similarly narrow) ideal that the chief virtue is obedience/self-denial and that faculties ought to be rooted out is misguided; human faculties were given to be cultivated and unfolded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote a conception of character that blends self-development and self-government rather than exclusive abnegation. Anti-pattern: religious or social doctrines that valorize uniform obedience at the cost of human capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of tastes requires institutional tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Because persons differ in tastes, susceptibilities, and conditions required for spiritual development, public sentiment and institutions must tolerate a wide diversity of modes of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid social penalties for merely doing 'what nobody does' or not doing 'what everybody does'; do not restrict personal practices simply because they are uncommon, provided they do not harm others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep channels open for novelty to prevent stagnation
rubrics_metrics.description: Society needs a minority of original persons whose experiments, if adopted, improve established practices; without them human life would become a stagnant pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect spaces where experimentation and novelty can arise (intellectual freedom, freedom of conduct). Anti-pattern: organizing education and public opinion so thoroughly that originality cannot breathe (historical example: China).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making the ideal of character 'to desire nothing strongly'
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard that prizes absence of marked character (weak desires and energies) leads to outward conformity without inner strength, producing weak, unenergetic persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value strong feelings guided by reason and conscience rather than anaemic conformity. Beware philanthropic or moral reforms that aim merely to make everyone moderate and similar rather than truly better.
